findings.scope: Actual main303/current8deda and latest B service; independently reproduced in process
findings.detail: Terminal bridge shutdown closes business admission but only drops fixed stdio/sink connections. The current remote lease remains valid; a late authenticated receipt is accepted and resolves an outstanding fact after shutdown, emitting a receipt frame. I reported this gap but its green shutdown test only observes pending for150ms and does not submit the late receipt.
findings.implication: Terminal callback settlement is not closed. This does not prove native writes bypass main current-command/answer admission; the measured counterexample concerns a fact receipt.
findings.repairDirection: Distinguish reconnectable transport loss from terminal teardown. Terminal shutdown must close/fence the actual current channel and pending callbacks; a deliberate ordinary handover can retain the reconnect semantics. Test late reply after terminal shutdown directly.

findings.scope: New unintegrated B caller only; not a current public main payload regression
findings.detail: The callback protocol uses payload-read.reference and replies with the original JSON value. The new caller instead reads request.ref, supplies absent offset/length as0, and replies with a chunk/base64 metadata object as value. An actual service payload read receives ref empty and returns the envelope instead of the frozen payload while served.payloads increments successfully.
findings.implication: Do not admit the new caller as a working three-callback adapter or integrate it for original Store/Broker recovery yet.
findings.repairDirection: Use the established coordinator payload callback contract/reference and original JSON semantics. Keep the separate journal descriptor/chunk replay protocol separate. Add actual payload and native-intent consumers alongside the current fact-only fixture.
